w:r.w:t: Lara is an escrow-powered payment app for social commerce. The first target market is Nigerian buyers and sellers who currently trade on WhatsApp, Instagram, Telegram, and similar channels where trust is weak and payment proof is easy to fake.

The job of Lara is to act as the trust layer. The app should let a seller create a protected order, let the buyer fund it, hold the money safely, and release the money only when the agreed delivery conditions are met.

Today the backend already supports user registration, login, wallet creation, internal wallet-to-wallet transfer, escrow order creation and funding, escrow status changes, disputes, refunds, Kora bank payout initiation, Quidax withdrawal initiation, idempotency for protected POST requests, and webhook recording for Kora and Quidax.

The app does not yet support Kora pay-ins to fund escrow directly, admin dispute resolution workflows, file uploads for proof or evidence, push notifications, a public top-up endpoint, internal crypto wallet balances, or a complete cross-border FX quote and lock flow.
Lara is not just a wallet app. Lara is a transaction orchestration and trust product built around escrow.
A seller should know that when Lara says an order is funded, the money is real.
A buyer should know that the seller cannot receive the money until delivery conditions are met.
Both parties should be able to see the status of the order clearly from creation to release, dispute, refund, or cancellation.
Kora is the fiat banking rail. Lara uses it for bank metadata and bank payouts today, and should later use it for collections, payment links, virtual accounts, and settlement.

Quidax is the secondary provider rail for crypto and the planned cross-border FX stability layer. The current backend includes Quidax withdrawal plumbing, but not a full internal crypto wallet or cross-border pricing engine yet.

The escrow model is the heart of the product.
Buyer funds that order from their Lara wallet.
The money moves from the buyer wallet into an escrow system wallet.
Seller marks the order as shipped.
Seller marks the order as delivered.
Buyer confirms delivery with a six-digit delivery code, or the order is auto-released after the confirmation deadline if no dispute is opened.
If the buyer disputes before release, the order moves into DISPUTED.
The seller can refund before release.
The buyer is not set when the seller creates the order.
The first buyer who successfully funds the order becomes the buyer for that order.
The seller cannot fund their own order.
Funding returns the delivery code in the response today.
There is no separate admin resolution endpoint yet.
There is no generated Kora payment link or virtual account for escrow funding yet.
